problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}-3?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}+2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start with plotting the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/27e33d04bccb0136877dce919662aa5f78bb8315e6b2931461419fc8bc1664bd.png)

Next, we plot the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}.$ To do this, we scale the graph above by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,\frac{1}{2})$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/d98570b1dc97924ccb9af8a252769f0873387b029dcd5f95be8be57942f2fb7a.png)

Finally, we plot the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}+2.$ To do this, we shift the above graph $2$ units up. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,\frac{1}{2})$ to $(0,\frac{5}{2})$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/2192d5153baf0170024880585d956aec347caedc0f8ac1aeda56e9a225675863.png)
